name: Bitcoin
summary: A peer-to-peer electronic cash system published as a nine-page paper with working code attached.
community_signal: A few dozen readers, most of them hostile or indifferent. The first substantive replies explained why it would not work.
why_dismissed: Digital cash had been tried repeatedly and had failed every time. DigiCash went bankrupt in 1998, e-gold was shut down, and the informed prior after a decade of failures was that this was a solved-and-abandoned problem.
dismissal_may_be_wrong_because: The prior was right about the failure mode and wrong about the mechanism. Every previous attempt had a central issuer that could be shut down or could inflate the supply. This one removed the issuer, which is precisely the thing that had killed the others, and the paper said so explicitly on the first page.
promote_criteria: Not applicable. Retained as the calibration entry for this file: the pattern to recognise is a working artifact plus a document plus a small hostile technical audience, publicly visible for years before any price existed.

name: RISC-V
summary: An open instruction set architecture begun as a teaching project at Berkeley.
community_signal: A single university research group, then a slow accretion of academic and embedded users over roughly a decade.
why_dismissed: Instruction sets were considered a settled duopoly. An open ISA with no compiler ecosystem, no toolchain maturity and no commercial backer was a teaching exercise, and the graveyard of alternative architectures was already large.
dismissal_may_be_wrong_because: The competitive question was never technical merit, it was licensing cost and supply chain control — and both of those changed for reasons external to the technology. It took roughly twelve years, which is the point of including it: this file is a slow instrument.
promote_criteria: Not applicable. Retained as a second calibration entry, showing the quiet decade-long version of the pattern rather than the dramatic one.

name: Fully Homomorphic Encryption
summary: Computation performed directly on encrypted data, so a processor can operate on information it cannot read.
venue: Cryptography research and a small number of open implementations
community_signal: Several competing open-source libraries with small but genuine developer communities. Check the commit recency as carefully as the star count — one of the leading repositories has not been pushed to in months, which is the more informative number.
why_dismissed: Too slow. The overhead against plaintext computation has historically been four to six orders of magnitude, which puts almost every application out of reach regardless of how valuable privacy is.
dismissal_may_be_wrong_because: The overhead has been falling steadily and hardware acceleration is being designed specifically for it. The relevant question is not whether the overhead is large but at what multiple the first application becomes viable, and whether the curve reaches it. That is a measurable question and nobody appears to be tracking it against a threshold.
promote_criteria: A named commercial deployment processing production data at a disclosed cost multiple, plus a published overhead series showing sustained decline. Then it earns a candidate_themes row and a cost_curves row.
kill_criteria: Overhead decline flattens for three consecutive years with no application below a 1000x multiple.

name: Autonomous Experimentation
summary: Closed-loop systems that design, run and interpret physical experiments without a human in the cycle.
community_signal: Small, institutionally scattered, and mostly publishing rather than shipping. No obvious community hub, which is itself a weakness in tracking it.
why_dismissed: Laboratory automation is decades old and has consistently underdelivered. Robots that pipette are not new, and the hard part of science was never the pipetting.
dismissal_may_be_wrong_because: If the hard part is hypothesis generation rather than execution, then this becomes interesting exactly when the generation side gets good — which is a recent change and not one the historical dismissal had available to it. This is the clearest case in the file of an old dismissal that may have been overtaken by an unrelated development.
promote_criteria: A materially valuable discovery — a compound, a material, a process — attributable to a closed loop rather than to a human who used automation as a tool. Attribution will be contested, so require the counterfactual to be stated.
kill_criteria: Five years of operation across multiple groups with no discovery that would not have been made conventionally.

name: Biological Computing Substrates
summary: Cultured neural tissue used as a computational medium.
venue: A handful of academic groups and two or three startups
community_signal: Extremely small. Single-digit numbers of serious groups worldwide.
why_dismissed: It is not obviously computing. The demonstrations are toy tasks that conventional silicon does trivially and vastly more cheaply, and the energy efficiency argument depends on comparisons that have not been made carefully.
dismissal_may_be_wrong_because: The energy argument, if it survives careful measurement, is not a marginal one — biological substrates operate several orders of magnitude below silicon for certain operations. That claim is either wrong or enormous, and it is currently untested rather than disproven. Included specifically because it is the entry most likely to be embarrassing, which is the correct composition for this file.
promote_criteria: A benchmarked task where the biological substrate beats silicon on energy per operation under measurement conditions a sceptic would accept.
kill_criteria: Careful independent measurement shows the energy advantage does not survive the full system boundary, including culture maintenance.

name: Prediction Markets
summary: Markets whose instruments settle on the truth of stated propositions, used as an information mechanism rather than as an asset class.
venue: Regulatory filings and a small trading community
community_signal: Small, and unusual for this file in being commercial rather than technical. That makes it the one entry whose community size is directly observable as traded volume rather than inferred from code activity.
why_dismissed: Persistently thin liquidity and an unresolved regulatory status that has repeatedly killed venues.
dismissal_may_be_wrong_because: The historical constraint was legal rather than technical or economic, and legal constraints change discontinuously. Thin liquidity is also partly an artefact of the legal constraint rather than an independent problem. This entry is here to test whether the framework can handle a candidate whose binding constraint is regulatory — the signal ladder currently instruments that poorly.
promote_criteria: Sustained liquidity in contracts that resolve on non-sporting, non-political propositions, indicating use as an information mechanism rather than as gambling.
kill_criteria: Volume remains concentrated in sports and elections for three more years, confirming it is an entertainment product.
